atoms:
"Merritronix is a genuinely growing, small, high-reliability electronics manufacturer, not a software-like defence IP platform. Its FY2026 revenue was ₹155.90 crore and restated profit ₹16.10 crore. The business has useful qualification history, real turnkey assembly revenue and customer relationships, but one customer supplied 62.08% of revenue. Component procurement, inventory and supplier advances absorb much of the apparent accounting profitability. [S1]

Verdict: **Hold — unresolved. Not eligible for numerical investment ranking or a compounder designation.** Provisional descriptive BQS is 5.2/10 and GQS 5.0/10 (raw 6.40, capped for persistent CASH2); IAS is NS. The decisive questions are the reliability of financial records and current executable market evidence, not a presumption that all SMEs are poor businesses. The full statutory audit annexures contain unresolved bank-return differences, absent audit trails and incomplete control documentation. The IPO restatement does explain profit differences; it must not be represented as an unexplained fraud. [S1, S2]

Fresh IPO proceeds of ₹70.03 crore materially improve the balance sheet. They are not ₹70.03 crore of freely distributable cash: machinery, working capital, debt repayment and issue costs use the same proceeds. A conservative end-June receipt model has a historical cash-floor gap of ₹5.44 crore before verified proceeds become available. A plausible earlier listing-date availability variant is fully funded and yields only 7.60% conditional annualized return at the ₹403.55 reference price, below the 15% hurdle. That timing contrast is not evidence of an actual default. All ordinary return and entry-price fields remain null because the reliability gate is unresolved. [S1, S8, S15]

The upside case requires customer diversification, conversion of qualifications into orders, commissioning of the IPO-funded equipment, sustained margins and substantial improvement in cash conversion. The downside does not require the end of Indian defence demand: one programme postponement, slower customer advances or inventory obsolescence can overwhelm the earnings narrative. A cheaper quote alone would not resolve the audit questions."

"Identity: Merritronix Ltd.; formerly Merritronix Private Limited, incorporated 14 October 1988 and converted to a public company on 7 February 2025. CIN in the reviewed documents is U32100TG1988PLC155611. Security: BSE SME code 544773, symbol MRTX, ISIN INE1RQS01010. The October 19 official interoperability master contains the matching ISIN and 17,484,854 shares, with a 1,000-share market lot. The ordinary exchange venue is BSE; NSE archive absence is not proof of no trading. [S1, S2, S14]

Information cutoff: 20 October 2026. Market reference: 19 October 2026, ₹403.55, supported by an actual dated secondary historical table and corroborating broker history. This is not authenticated BSE bhavcopy closing evidence. Data retrieved after the cutoff are used only for documents published on or before it; October 21 prices are excluded. Entry and terminal dates are 19 October 2026 and 19 October 2031. All investor cash-flow discounting uses ACT/365.25 over the same 1,826 days. Assumed nominal, pretax equity hurdle is 15%; 12% and 18% are sensitivities. The ₹500,000 position is illustrative, not a portfolio instruction. [S14–S17]

G1 is a conditional pass: disclosed historic lending/deposit compliance failures were repaid, while current related-party advances require scrutiny. G2 is Hold — unresolved: financial reporting and bank-return reconciliation are materially insufficient. G3 is a conditional pass, not a declaration of pristine liquidity: known IPO resources can fund a credible timing path, but exact debt settlement and cash timing remain unverified and conservative stresses require funding. G4 is Hold — unresolved: lot size is verified, current restrictions/spreads and official BSE turnover are not. Ranking flags are false for BQS, GQS and IAS while G2 is unresolved.

Confidence is High for the existence and wording of the reviewed disclosures and Medium for economic comparability of the financial series. It is Low for exact current cash availability, executable market liquidity and an actionable valuation. Older statutory figures and FY24–26 restated figures are never silently mixed. FY22 CFO, ten-year history, dollar-weighted customer retention, product ASPs and current loan confirmations are ND rather than zero. The October H1 update contains unaudited management sales only, not a new audited profit or cash-flow period. [S1–S10]"

"All thirteen factors use the same v 3.0 definitions as main-board research. GOV measures governance; GQS is Growth Quality, not governance. P measures price-implied expectations, not simply cheapness. Each factor has sourced facts, contrary evidence and a stated uncertainty. R and L are genuinely unscored; neither is assigned a neutral five.

BQS raw and final arithmetic is 5.16: GOV4×20% + MOAT5×20% + REV8×12% + DUR6×10% + CAP6×12% + CASH2×10% + BAL5×8% + EXEC6×8%. Half-up display is 5.2. GQS raw is 6.40: REV8×40% + DUR6×20% + EARN6×15% + CAP6×15% + CASH2×10%. Persistent poor cash realization gives CASH2 and activates the framework growth-quality cap: final GQS5.00, display 5.0. These are descriptive diagnostics with full arithmetic coverage, not eligible rankings under the unresolved G2 gate.

IAS uses Q=5.16, not rounded 5.2: known contribution is 5.16×25% + D3×20% + P3×10% =2.19. Missing R35% and L10% leave 55% coverage. The mathematical 1–10 missing-factor bound is 2.64–6.69; it is neither an estimated IAS nor a confidence interval. IAS remains NS.

REV starts at 9 for the preferred five-year 65.62% sales CAGR, then is capped at 8 because volume/mix comparability is not High confidence. Six-year and three-year corroboration support the direction; there is no discretionary small-base penalty or bonus for a very large TAM. CAP6 reflects a coherent stable-perimeter return bridge and mixed recurrence, not a requirement to see private project accounts. CASH2 is an evidenced conversion weakness, not a penalty for unavailable numbers. GOV4 does not activate the GOV≤3 cap; a downgrade to 3 would require new evidence and the cap would be applied explicitly.

Joint ±1 sensitivity in GOV and CAP moves uncapped BQS from 4.84 to 5.48. If GOV3 were supported by sufficient adverse evidence, final BQS and IAS would be capped at 3 and the governance classification would override; this is not the baseline finding. R cannot be filled from an algebraic terminal value after a cash-floor breach. A funded, hypothetical timing alternative is retained separately but does not cure G2."

"The operating chain is component sourcing and qualification, surface-mount and through-hole PCB assembly, inspection, testing, box-build integration and delivery. Automated optical inspection, X-ray and functional testing matter because failures in aerospace and defence systems can be costly. Some mechanical enclosure work is bought from third parties. Jobs are tied to customer designs, technical specifications, acceptance tests and purchase orders rather than an owned software subscription or an exclusive end-product brand. [S1]

FY26 turnkey/build-to-print revenue was ₹143.5301 crore,92.07% of sales; obsolescence procurement/engineering ₹10.1802 crore,6.53%; trading ₹0.9955 crore,0.64%; and jobwork ₹1.1898 crore,0.76%. In FY25 turnkey was 82.64%, trading 7.31% and obsolescence 8.07%. This shift changes both the economic content of reported sales and working-capital demand. Jobwork customers supply materials; turnkey revenue includes the purchased components. Gross sales are therefore not equivalent to manufacturing value added. [S1]

Obsolescence work can include finding unavailable components, reverse engineering and redesign support for legacy platforms. It may earn superior margins, but component procurement is still part of the service. The reviewed evidence does not establish a recurring royalty portfolio or a large base of product IP owned by Merritronix. Analinear and Stuam cooperation may widen design capability; no consideration, order value or separately recognized revenue was disclosed. These are development options, not sales already won. [S1, S11]

Aerospace/defence represented 97.81% of FY26 sector exposure. Approximately 92% of business was with private counterparties rather than direct government organizations. The ultimate programme may be governmental while Merritronix still bears the payment, acceptance and credit risk of a private customer. Approved-vendor status with prominent organizations demonstrates qualification, not an unconditional sovereign payment promise. Geographic exports were only about ₹0.5734 crore in FY26; domestic procurement/programme risk dominates. [S2, S9]

There are no reported operating subsidiaries, minority claims or acquisitions creating a consolidated earnings step-up in the reviewed period. Related entities in the RPT notes are not automatically subsidiaries. The growth analysis follows the legal standalone company and separately recognizes that telecom kits were discontinued and the revenue mix shifted toward turnkey manufacturing. [S1, S2]"

"The favorable case rests on accumulated manufacturing process knowledge, quality documentation, customer qualification and experience with long-lived defence/aerospace platforms. Requalifying another supplier may involve testing costs and delays. EN9100 certification and the ability to handle complex PCB assemblies create a real entry hurdle above commodity trading. Repeat-customer counts and established engagements are evidence of commercial access. They do not by themselves prove pricing power. [S1, S9]

The detailed FY26 customer table gives the top customer 62.08% of revenue, top three 80.11%, top five 89.36% and top ten 97.69%. The early risk table reports 80.11/89.36% under top-five/top-ten labels. We retain both and use the more complete business table rather than suppress the inconsistency. The leading customer is anonymized in that table; it is not automatically assigned to a named customer elsewhere in the presentation. A count of 79 active customers is compatible with very high revenue concentration. Sixty-eight were repeat customers,86.08% by count, not net-dollar retention. [S1]

About 73.92% of revenue was associated with longer-term arrangements, but the prospectus says most customer contracts do not commit minimum volumes and purchase orders can vary. Qualification may reduce switching without preventing price negotiation, order deferral, customer insourcing or programme completion. A heavily material-intensive cost base can also pass through raw-material deflation as lower gross revenue. Claims of moat should therefore be tested against retained business, margin resilience, accepted deliveries and collection, not only certification logos. [S1]

Closest economic comparators are qualified EMS specialists, not consumer brands or asset-light software. The RHP lists Centum and Vinyas: the former's disclosed FY26 profitability was negative, while Vinyas used a FY25 comparator. These mixed-period figures and May 15 prices cannot be averaged into a cutoff-date peer PE. Cyient DLM is a larger, parent-supported, more international consolidated business with an acquisition history. Its FY26 revenue decline after a major defence programme finished is a useful warning that qualifications do not prevent programme cyclicality. Its different perimeter, leases and customer mix limit direct valuation transfer. [S1, S18]

MOAT5 is consequently a middle assessment: established capabilities and relationships, but no demonstrated durable monopoly over customer economics. Evidence of improved concentration and stable value-added margin through a difficult procurement cycle would support an upgrade; loss of a major programme or qualification would weaken it."

"Revenue rose from ₹13.5906 crore in FY20 to ₹12.5115 crore in FY21, ₹16.4891 crore in FY22, ₹53.1738 crore in FY23, ₹85.6991 crore in FY24, ₹113.5638 crore in FY25 and ₹155.8956 crore in FY26. The preferred five-year FY21–26 CAGR is 65.62%; the six-year FY20–26 cross-check is 50.18% and FY23–26 is 43.12%. FY21 was a pandemic-period year, but its approximately 7.9% fall alone does not justify inventing a quantified volume distortion or choosing a more favorable window. [S1, S3, S5, S6]

The absolute FY25 and FY26 additions were ₹27.8647 and ₹42.3318 crore. This is meaningful scaling, not merely a percentage on a negligible final base. No acquisition contribution is disclosed. However, the very large FY23 step-up, discontinued telecom kits, growing turnkey share and changing component content mean that legal-perimeter organic growth is not the same thing as constant-mix unit growth. Product units and realized ASPs by programme are not disclosed. The historical model therefore shows material-adjusted value-added revenue as a cross-check, without calling it an audited segment or inventing volume/price percentages. [S1, S3, S5]

H1FY27 management sales were ₹106.37 crore, up 90.15%. The implied comparative half was about ₹55.94 crore, but neither the implied comparator nor doubling the latest half is an audited TTM earnings series. H1 sales already exceed half of FY26 full-year sales by a substantial amount. This provides a reasonable demand anchor for FY27 scenario sales of ₹180/210/235 crore, while also showing that the base assumes a slower second half than the first. No full-year management EPS has been manufactured from that update. [S10]

The durability test is not whether these growth rates were exciting; it is whether growth continues to generate acceptable returns after procurement, receivables, deposits, customer-advance changes and dilution. Gross sales growth that requires permanent financing at unattractive cost is not sufficient. Conversely, the absence of product-level ASP data does not erase the demonstrated absolute revenue growth. REV8 balances both points and remains separate from the lower CASH score."

"At March 26, installed annual capacity was 1.075 million SMT boards,0.600 million through-hole boards and 0.420 million box-build units. These are different process stages and potentially the same final product; summing them to 2.095 million does not produce a defensible sales-capacity denominator. The January 26 Panasonic line raised SMT nameplate capacity from 0.765 million. The July presentation uses 0.8425 million weighted capacity and 82.94% utilization, compared with the unweighted 65% figure. Through-hole and box-build utilization were approximately 99% and 98.93%. The October update still cites the older SMT capacity/utilization combination, so a consistent capacity date and basis must be requested. [S1, S9, S10]

The ₹21.36 crore IPO equipment budget is real financing, but June utilization was zero for this object. October management said ordering/delivery was underway and installation expected by end-calendar 2026. New equipment must be installed, validated, qualified, loaded with orders, delivered and accepted before it generates revenue. Neither a machinery order nor an NADCAP discussion is commercial revenue. The scenario model does not invent a uniform rupee-per-board ASP. Base/bull revenue growth remains an analyst programme/mix assumption, checked against existing utilization and backlog; its missing bottom-up product conversion is explicitly a limitation. [S8–S10]

Backlog was ₹96.6491 crore at April 30, ₹98.06 crore in July presentation and ₹101.64 crore at September 30. Against FY27 base sales ₹210 crore, the September book covers approximately 48.4% of one year's sales, without adjustment for delivery dates or cancellation. The leading April order-book customer had ₹50.5703 crore,52.32% of the book. Revenue recognition plus modest backlog growth suggests new intake, but a complete intake/execution/cancellation bridge is not disclosed and no exact order-intake figure is claimed. [S1, S9, S10]

Using financing-side invested capital, the model includes equity plus debt less cash/deposits plus a required operating-cash reserve. Working capital and related advances remain invested, not discarded as non-operating merely because they hurt the return. At the stated normal 29.12% tax rate, FY24–26 incremental NOPAT/capital is 28.09%; FY25–26 is 21.93%. The two-year scale-only result at the original EBIT margin is 6.88%. A12% midcycle EBIT-margin endpoint gives 17.12%, around the 14–18% analyst capital-cost range rather than overwhelmingly above it. Most incremental earnings came from margin/mix improvement, so the bridge does not prove that every new machine earns the headline return. [S1]

Final GQS is capped at 5 under the persistent CASH2 override despite raw 6.40. CAP6 and DUR6 are therefore mixed-positive, not NS: the aggregate bridge is coherent and economically informative. Future evidence should show project ramp-up, stable normalized margins, inventory turns, third-party orders and cash collection. The explicit six-month capacity/qualification delay stress cuts FY27 second-half sales 20%, slows FY28 growth to 10%, reduces EBITDA margin to 13%, raises operating working capital to 52% of sales and adds 20% capex overrun. It does not merely postpone spending while preserving all the revenue."

"The founder-led business has operated since 1988 and the IPO was entirely a fresh issue: ₹70.03 crore goes to the company, not an offer-for-sale exit by promoters. Promoter ownership was 85.16% before the IPO and approximately 62.28% after it. FY26 director remuneration was ₹0.371 crore, not intrinsically excessive relative to earnings. These are favorable facts, but concentrated control still makes related-party transactions and reporting discipline important. Current September share-pledge changes were not independently authenticated, so “nil current pledge” is not asserted. [S1, S2, S8]

Sunrise Telecom, a promoter/director proprietorship, had ₹4.8446 crore of supplier/trade advances outstanding. This is approximately 9.12% of restated equity and 30.09% of restated PAT. Total disclosed related-party purchases were ₹2.6558 crore. Earlier director loans were recovered and a ₹4.25 crore capital advance was refunded in FY25; small advances/recoveries with other related entities are separately disclosed. Recovery of old exposures is positive, but it does not establish independent pricing or timely delivery on today's larger supplier advance. A commercial advance is not automatically an unlawful loan. Required follow-up is ageing, purchase linkage, delivery, independent approval, comparable terms and subsequent settlement. [S1, S2]

The IPO examiner expressly recorded FY24 loans to related parties inconsistent with Section 185 and acceptance of loans from nonmember individuals inconsistent with deposit rules. Both were fully repaid and the examiner states no continuing noncompliance as of its report. That remediation is preserved. The statutory main audit, CARO, cost-record and audit-trail problems described below nevertheless show that formal governance has not kept pace with growth. No allegation of fraud is made solely from these inconsistencies. [S1, S2]

Auditor Chengalrayulu resigned in November 2023 citing preoccupation; Dagliya was appointed in March 2024. The reviewed evidence does not establish an information-denial resignation. The FY26 auditor did not resign. The IPO examination refers to a May 04 underlying FY26 audit and no qualifications requiring restatement, whereas the annual statutory report is dated May 14 and uses undefined except-for wording. The issuer and auditor should reconcile the documents rather than investors simply choosing the cleaner version. [S1, S2, S6]

Execution is assessed against events: January SMT commissioning is reported complete; the fresh IPO and June deployment are completed financing events; the post-IPO machinery was still being ordered/delivered in October. The design-partner MoUs have no quantified commercial order value. The H1 revenue update is management-estimated, not audited cash realization. Appointment of an IR agency and a secretarial auditor is governance infrastructure, not proof that accounting weaknesses are repaired. EXEC6 recognizes actual delivery without promoting plans into achieved earnings. [S8–S11]"

"**Scope and earnings.** FY24–26 restated sales are ₹85.6991/113.5638/155.8956 crore; restated PAT₹3.0503/8.6595/16.1030 crore. Statutory FY26 PAT₹15.4849 crore is reconciled to ₹16.1030 crore through ₹0.6899 crore reversal of prior-period items, ₹0.1745 crore adverse deferred-tax adjustment and ₹0.1027 crore current-tax adjustment. FY25 and FY24 have their own detailed interest, chit-income, depreciation, gratuity, lease and tax reclassifications. Interest on late tax is not necessarily an omitted operating expense. Opening net-worth and profit reconciliation are embedded; the existence of differences is not a standalone misconduct finding. [S1, S2]

**CFO bridge.** FY24–26 restated CFO was ₹4.5324/−6.6433/−23.3821 crore, totaling−₹25.4930 crore against ₹27.8128 crore PAT, or−91.66% conversion. FY26 cash absorbed ₹31.6214 crore inventory, ₹16.1247 crore receivables and ₹7.3807 crore advances, partly offset by ₹9.6363 crore payables and ₹6.5612 crore other current liabilities. The latter includes substantial customer advances, whose continued growth is not a permanent free source of funding. FY25 payable settlement also caused a large cash outflow. [S1]

The statutory FY26 CFO−₹13.9409 crore differs from restated−₹23.3821 crore by−₹9.4412 crore. A line-by-line arithmetic bridge is pre-working-capital−₹0.3416 crore, working-capital−₹12.3590 crore and tax-payment deduction+₹3.2594 crore. CFI changes−₹0.0358 crore and CFF+₹0.4118 crore; the total−₹9.0652 crore matches the narrower restated closing cash definition. Statutory closing cash ₹25.6963 crore includes deposits, versus restated cash equivalents ₹16.6311 crore, while opening definitions differ. Statutory cash-flow depreciation ₹0.9195 crore conflicts with statutory P&L₹0.4718 crore; the restated CF uses ₹0.4718 crore. FY25 CFO differs−₹4.7065 crore, with ₹4.25 crore capital-advance refund moved to investing and ₹0.4271 crore financing difference. These arithmetic/classification bridges explain much of the structure but are not an issuer-certified economic reconciliation of every line. [S1, S2]

Other-bank and long-term deposit changes sit in the restated cash-flow classifications. Removing the netFY26₹7.7977 crore deposit-placement effect improves CFO to−₹15.5844 crore; after cash interest and capex, owner FCF remains−₹21.7295 crore. The cash-conversion criticism therefore survives a favorable classification adjustment. Five-year CFO conversion is ND because FY22 CFO was unavailable in the retrieved annual file; it is not filled with zero. [S1, S4]

**Full audit annexures.** The FY26 main opinion says except for effects of the matter in Basis for Opinion, but that basis identifies no specific qualification. The auditor did not have the directors' report when issuing its report. Audit trail was not maintained despite applicability since April 2023. Cost records required under law were not supplied for verification, although the directors' report says they were maintained. IFC is opined effective while explicitly stating there was no written internal-control framework and relying on inquiry, observation and other procedures. These are materially weaker facts than an uncomplicated “clean audit.” [S2]

Annual-report CARO says bank returns agree but its Q4 Axis table shows book-versus-bank differences of−₹0.0597 crore inventory,−₹0.0350 crore receivables and−₹1.4665 crore payables. The RHP's wider CSB schedule discloses FY26 Q2 stock+₹24.9930 crore and debtors+₹21.4814 crore, and Q4 stock+₹10.9692 crore. It explains purchase entries after submission, corrected debtor grouping and a TDS entry. FY24/25 also show differences. The explanation is relevant counterevidence, but corrected bank submissions and reconciliation between the two documents' bank/quarter tables were not verified. The direction and magnitude do not, by themselves, establish borrowing inflation or fraud. [S1, S2]

Old undisputed professional-tax/income-tax-interest/TDS dues total ₹0.0896 crore; a ₹0.6369 crore GST appeal is separately disclosed despite generic no-disputed-dues wording. No fraud, debt default, FY26 auditor resignation or cash loss was reported. Physical-inventory discrepancies were not 10% or more by class; the auditor did not identify uncertainty about meeting one-year liabilities. These favorable observations are retained, not discarded because other parts are adverse. G2 remains unresolved because the combined record is insufficiently reliable for an investable earnings/cash conclusion. [S2]

**Funding.** March 26 debt ₹43.1974 crore includes ₹15.2295 crore cash credit and ₹20 crore short-tenor SIDBI facilities, not just ordinary ₹1.5 crore annual amortization. The ₹14.5 crore loan was disbursed March 31 for three months; the prospectus still shows the full amount at April 30, making a simple April instalment assertion unsafe. Main modeling retires it by June 30; an earlier-instalment stress is separate. The ₹5.5 crore nine-month facility originated November 20,2025 and is retired by the August interval. Opening on-demand non-CC debt ₹0.8683 crore is conservatively repaid in April; residual current term maturities are modeled through recurring principal. [S1, S2]

Gross IPO₹70.03 crore is allocated once: ₹21.36 crore machinery, ₹21.95 crore working capital, ₹12.72 crore debt, ₹7.91 crore GCP and ₹6.09 crore fees. June use was ₹12.16 crore WC, ₹8.80 crore debt and ₹5.94 crore fees; ₹43.13 crore remained, versus ₹43.14 crore in the deployment table due rounding. The ₹7.91 crore GCP parked in a cash-credit account is modeled as a CC offset, with no second free-cash addition and no automatic redraw. Its inability to be redrawn is an analytical conservatism, not a proved legal restriction. The ₹15 crore IPO FD remains earmarked; premature eligible use is tested against a maturity-lock alternative. [S8]

The June loan allocation is inferred within disclosed object budgets: ₹3.9 crore against the first SIDBI loan and ₹4.9 crore against the second, followed by ₹3.32 crore other eligible debt in July and ₹0.6 crore SIDBI in August. Actual loan-specific June remittances are not disclosed. The model therefore cannot certify historical solvency from private bank movements. Conservative end-June receipt gives a ₹5.44 crore base reserve gap; June 8 assumed availability yields none. Neither sequence is labeled an observed default. Original tax ₹6.8224 crore, old dues and accrued interest are removed from operating capital where necessary and paid once; gratuity remains a terminal claim. Prepaid IPO cost is bounded 0–₹0.9753 crore, base ₹0.6 crore, never expensed twice. Liens on FDs are not repeatedly summed when the same security is described under multiple loans. [S1, S2, S8]"

"At the dated secondary ₹403.55 reference and 17,484,854 shares, market capitalization is ₹705.60 crore. Restated FY26 current-share-equivalent EPS is ₹9.21, giving 43.82× earnings; statutory profit gives 45.57×. Weighted historical EPS and bonus-adjusted comparators cannot be substituted for the current denominator. March pre-IPO equity gives 13.28× book, but this is explicitly not current post-IPO PB. A March-debt/cash EV cross-check is about 26.90× FY26 EBITDA; it is likewise not a certified October EV. H1 sales without PAT do not support an audited TTM PE. [S1, S2, S14–S16]

Three full cash-flow scenarios extend through the exact October 2031 horizon. Base FY27 sales ₹210 crore then grow 20/18/15/12/10%; EBITDA margin 15%, operating working capital 46% of sales, recurring capex 2% and D&A1.5%. Bear uses ₹180 crore, then 0/5/5/5/5%,10% margin,58% working capital,2% recurring capex,20% machinery overrun and inventory/related-advance/GST stresses. Bull uses ₹235 crore, then 30/25/22/18/15%,18% margin,40% working capital and 2.5% recurring capex. These are analyst scenarios, not company guidance. Cash rent is already in operating margins; no capitalized lease liability is deducted again. Normal cash tax 29.12% follows the prospectus regime. No operating factory property is added on top of earnings EV. [S1, S2, S8, S10]

Exit EV/EBITDA assumptions are 10×/16×/22×. Main conservative timing paths all have an earlier funding gap, so **every non-rescue conditional return and entry price is null**, as well as every ordinary return. Terminal prices in the model are algebraic diagnostics only, not realizable returns on an unfunded path. A June 8 assumed-availability base variant is fully funded and yields 7.60%; its 15%-hurdle entry diagnostic is ₹289.40. This is conditional on timing and all other assumptions, not an actionable buy price while G2 remains unresolved.

Separate rescues issue whole shares at an assumed ₹250 with 2% fees before each interval's uses. Base/bear/bull hypothetical gross proceeds are ₹5.55/₹22.61/₹4.55 crore. These are not committed financing. Pre-entry issuance is distinguished from post-entry dilution, and ownership dilution from share-count expansion. The source record does not say such rescues occurred.

DCF is a cross-check on cash economics, not a way to hide dependence on the exit multiple. It uses the explicit post-entry FCFF schedule,14/16/18% WACC,3/4/5% terminal growth and 18% terminal ROIC including required cash. It includes remaining earmarked funds once because corresponding eligible future uses are deducted in FCFF. Debt, retained cash reserve and employee claims are included consistently. The 9-point DCF range is ₹70.84–₹114.41 per share, far below the exit-multiple story, with high terminal-value concentration. This disagreement is an economic warning about cash intensity and terminal assumptions, not a reason to average incompatible methods into false precision.

Reverse expectations scan post-FY27 constant growth across 0–50% and require a genuinely funded hurdle crossing. Under conservative timing there is no eligible solution; a separate earlier-receipt reverse scan also tests whether higher growth can be funded. Neither returns a fully funded 15% crossing under these assumptions, and no endpoint is reported as a required growth rate. Full two-way growth/multiple, working-capital/margin, capex/amortization, reserve, tax, FD-lock, receipt-timing, CC-recall and hurdle rows are embedded. P3 reflects demanding priced-in assumptions; R remains NS."

"A credible adverse path is a major customer's acceptance or purchase-order delay while parts and work-in-process have already been bought. With 62.08% revenue concentration, the loss need not be industry-wide. Inventory then ages, cash collection slows and customer advances stop growing. Suppliers and lenders still require payment; bespoke or obsolete components may have limited resale value. A10% cash replacement/write-down stress on March 26 inventory,50% loss on the Sunrise advance and the disclosed GST dispute are modeled as separate one-time cash pressures, not assertions that those losses have occurred. [S1, S2]

The bear assumesFY27 sales ₹180 crore with a flat FY28,10% EBITDA margin and 58% operating working capital/sales. The model keeps recurring capex after the IPO budget expires and delays the new capacity instead of assuming a free expansion. It preserves cash reserves, debt claims and a haircut to residual deposits at exit. The maximum prefunding gap is ₹22.16 crore under the conservative receipt sequence. Unfunded terminal equity is not offered as an investor return.

A separately financed bear needs ₹22.61 crore gross equity at ₹250, with 2% fees and whole shares. Its hypothetical funded return is-20.49%. This illustrates severe capital-loss potential even after financing is supplied; it does not establish that a rescue will be available. An equity issue below the current quote transfers substantial economics to new funders, and repeated issues would worsen old-holder outcomes.

Further stress cases retire CC instead of assuming renewal, accelerate term principal to ₹5/10 crore annually, lock IPO FDs until maturity and raise working-capital intensity while cutting margins. The ₹18 crore rated CC limit compared with ₹15.2295 crore March draw suggests potential ₹2.7705 crore headroom, but it is not treated as an automatic committed undrawn line without current sanction conditions. The base's no-redraw treatment of the GCP credit balance is conservative, not a finding that the bank legally forbids access. [S1, S12]

Permanent-loss protection would come from diversified customers, cash collections, recoverable advances, transparent bank reconciliations and demonstrably available funding. Certifications, a large national defence budget and an attractive order announcement cannot substitute for those protections. D3 captures these risks without claiming an observed insolvency or fraud."

"Fivefold share-price appreciation from ₹403.55 requires ₹2,017.75 per share and tenfold requires ₹4,035.50 before distributions. Over the exact five-calendar-year horizon, those outcomes require approximately 38.0% and 58.5% annualized shareholder returns. The outcome test starts with the current post-IPO share count and explicitly shows what earnings or enterprise value would be needed at several terminal multiples, rather than assuming the current PE survives forever.

At 25× terminal PE and no further dilution, fivefold value requires about ₹141.12 crore PAT and tenfold about ₹282.24 crore. Against ₹16.103 crore restated FY26 PAT, that is approximately 8.76× and 17.53× profit, before accounting for the capital needed to support growth. At an illustrative 10% PAT margin, required sales are approximately ₹1,411 crore and ₹2,822 crore. These are arithmetic requirements, not forecasts. Greater dilution raises the aggregate earnings hurdle; a lower terminal multiple raises it further. [S1, S14, S15]

The current physical capacity, September backlog ₹101.64 crore, customer concentration and negative operating conversion do not substantiate such a scale-up within five years. Even the bull scenario requires sustained 30/25/22/18/15% post-FY27 growth,18% EBITDA margin, working-capital improvement and a 22× exit multiple. New lines, design partnerships, exports and obsolescence engineering could create options, but each must become funded, profitable commercial orders. The model does not count approval, pilot work or a nonbinding MoU as a booked recurring sales stream. [S9–S11]

Verdict on 5×/10×: mathematically possible in an extreme scaling outcome, not presently evidence-supported. This is not a statement that the stock cannot rise sharply in an SME market; price movement and durable cash-generating business compounding are different propositions."

"1. Obtain the auditor's clarification of the undefined except-for wording and the May 04/May 14 report relationship. Require a complete statutory-to-restated CFO reconciliation, including depreciation, cash/deposit definitions, tax paid and investing/financing reclassifications. Trigger: an unresolved adverse qualification or unexplained material discrepancy keeps G2 on Hold; a clean response must be specific, not generic “no fraud” language. [S1, S2]

2. Reconcile each quarter's bank stock/debtor/payable statements with books, including the FY26₹24.993/21.4814 crore Q2 differences and ₹10.9692 crore Q4 stock difference. Seek dated corrected bank submissions and matching balances, not only an explanation of purchase timing. Confirm audit-trail enablement, cost-record availability and an appropriately documented control framework. [S1, S2]

3. Track the ₹4.8446 crore Sunrise advance by ageing, purchase order, delivery, settlement and independent approval. Escalation trigger: unexplained growth, rollover without goods, related-party write-off or terms materially worse than comparable vendors. Confirm old statutory dues and GST appeal disposition without adding contingent and provisioned amounts twice. [S1, S2]

4. Read the audited/reviewed H1FY27 financials when issued. Reconcile the ₹106.37 crore management sales estimate, margins, cash taxes, CFO, inventory, receivables, customer advances and debt. Positive thesis evidence would be profitable growth with materially improved cash conversion, not merely a higher revenue number. Five-year CFO remains ND until the missing historic statement is located. [S4, S10]

5. Obtain September and later IPO-monitoring statements, bank balances and loan-specific repayments. Match the ₹14.5/5.5 crore short-tenor facilities, actual June debt deployment, FD liens/maturities and GCP cash-credit balance. Establish the real timing that made the completed IPO funding bridge work. Do not infer default from an analyst cash-floor stress or available finance from an unconfirmed credit line. [S1, S2, S8]

6. Verify machinery installation, acceptance and commercial qualification against the end-CY2026 expectation. Reconcile 0.765/1.075 million SMT capacity disclosures. Require line/product throughput and accepted revenue rather than counting each process-stage unit twice. For design MoUs and NADCAP discussions, track signed commercial orders, customer-funded development, delivery and cash. [S9–S11]

7. Track top-customer and top-five revenue, order-book ageing, execution/cancellations and repeat revenue by value. A larger customer count does not by itself diversify sales. A cancellation affecting the leading programme or dependence on continued large customer advances is a material downside trigger. [S1]

8. Before any implementation, obtain official BSE dated prices/turnover, current trading restrictions, lot, market-maker obligations and an observable two-sided spread. Re-run whole-lot participation at 2/5/10% and test orderly exit under adverse liquidity. No action is recommended from secondary volume alone. [S14–S17]"

"Final classification is Hold — unresolved. This is not a recommendation to buy or an instruction for an existing holder to trade. The company is not currently designated a proven compounder. Strong historical sales growth and potentially useful qualifications coexist with weak conversion, highly concentrated customers and unresolved financial-record questions. A fully computable score does not override a gate.

BQS5.2 and capped GQS5.0 (raw 6.40) are provisional descriptive assessments; neither enters the numerical quality ranking while G2 is unresolved. IAS and supported R are NS. G1 and G3 are conditional passes, preserving the favorable evidence of repaid historic loans, no reported fraud/default, completed fresh IPO and a funded plausible cash-timing alternative. G2 and G4 remain unresolved. No negative funding scenario is relabeled an actual default, and no unknown factor receives a neutral score.

Reassessment requires primary reconciliation of the audit/bank-return questions and a reliable contemporary financial/cash bridge. Demonstrated conversion of revenue into cash and settlement of the related supplier advance matter more than a press release about market size. Official market evidence is separately required before liquidity scoring or position sizing. A reduction in price can improve expected-return mathematics but cannot by itself repair unreliable inputs.

At present the appropriate analytical action is to retain the company on a monitored research list, with no investable return claim. If the questions are resolved, rerun the full dated funding and valuation models, update all thirteen factors under the same framework, and only then compare it with main-board and other SME opportunities. Current or future securities transactions require a separate investor decision; the illustrative position is not an allocation recommendation."
